title: Pollution ka Solution – Aaj Tak
source_file: Evaluation Parameters for Aaj Tak PkS-1.pdf

evaluation_note.central_question: If Delhi actually implements this, how much difference can it make to pollution?

impact_dimensions.name: Magnitude
impact_dimensions.question: How much pollution can potentially be reduced?

impact_dimensions.name: Coverage
impact_dimensions.question: How many people/areas/sources can it affect?

impact_dimensions.name: Duration
impact_dimensions.question: Is the benefit temporary or sustained?

impact_dimensions.name: Pollutants addressed
impact_dimensions.question: Does it address PM2.5/PM10, NOx, SOx, VOCs, waste, water contamination, noise, etc.?

impact_dimensions.name: Source significance
impact_dimensions.question: Does it tackle a major contributor or a relatively insignificant source?

delhi_reality_test: Does it solve a real Delhi problem? It is not merely a theoretical environmental problem.
Can it work under Delhi's conditions? Climate, density, traffic, infrastructure, governance, behaviour, etc.
Can it be implemented within existing institutional structures? Or does it require major legislative/institutional restructuring?
Can it eventually be scaled? A solution that works at one location but becomes prohibitively expensive at city scale should be scored accordingly.

evaluation_parameters.jury_should_ask: If implemented, how significant could the reduction in pollution be? Does it address a major source, pollutant or hotspot, or only a marginal problem?

Is the underlying science or technology sound? Is there credible evidence that the proposed intervention will produce the claimed result? Can this actually work in Delhi's real-world conditions—not merely in a laboratory or presentation? What infrastructure, permissions, behaviour or institutional changes are required?
Can it move from a pilot to city-wide implementation? Can it be replicated across Delhi/NCR and potentially other Indian cities?
What does it cost relative to the pollution reduction achieved? Is it financially viable for Government, citizens and/or industry?
Is the idea genuinely new, or does it provide a significantly better way of solving an existing problem?

scoring_matrix.score_1_weak: Limited or unclear impact; addresses a relatively small problem
scoring_matrix.score_3_moderate: Meaningful reduction in a defined pollution source/area
scoring_matrix.score_5_exceptional: Potential for substantial, measurable reduction in a significant pollution source

scoring_matrix.score_1_weak: Not valid scientifically; Difficult to implement under real-world Delhi conditions
scoring_matrix.score_5_exceptional: Scientific, Highly practical, realistic and implementable under existing conditions

scoring_matrix.score_1_weak: Works only at very limited scale
scoring_matrix.score_3_moderate: Can be expanded with substantial additional resources
scoring_matrix.score_5_exceptional: Can be rapidly scaled across Delhi/NCR and replicated elsewhere

scoring_matrix.score_1_weak: High cost relative to likely benefit
scoring_matrix.score_5_exceptional: Excellent pollution reduction per rupee invested; economically compelling

scoring_matrix.score_3_moderate: Some new element or meaningful adaptation
scoring_matrix.score_5_exceptional: Genuinely novel or transformative approach to the problem

final_check.relevance: Does the proposal demonstrably address a pollution problem?
final_check.credibility: Is there a scientifically/technically plausible mechanism through which it can reduce pollution?
final_check.testability: Can the claimed benefit be objectively tested and measured?
